articles.title: Jimmy Tata accuses Noel of 'backdoor takeover'
articles.description: Jimmy Naval Tata, younger brother of late Ratan Tata and one of the longest-serving trustees of Sir Ratan Tata Trust (SRTT), has accused Noel Tata of using the charitable institutions to consolidate family control over Tata Sons, calling the induction of multiple family members into the trusts a “back-door takeover” of the group’s holding company.In a detailed written response to a senior trustee on the state of affairs at Tata Trusts and controversies surrounding the group, Jimmy has also criticised changes to Tata Sons’ Articles of Association, backed chairman N Chandrasekaran’s reappointment and called on the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) to enforce the listing of Tata Sons without delay.Also Read: Jimmy Tata breaks silence on Tata matters; backs Chandra staying chair & Tata Sons listing, opposing Noel's stance“What has transpired in recent time is that the trusts are being filled with family members of the present Tata Trust Chairman, thereby securing a degree of control over Tata Sons that was never the settlors’ intention,” he said, adding that having more than one family member on a trust was inappropriate.“Such an arrangement is untenable and amounts to a back-door takeover of Tata Sons,” he said.Jimmy’s intervention is significant as the 85-year-old trustee has largely stayed away from trust meetings and voting and has rarely publicly articulated his views on the ongoing differences within the group.He said the two principal Tata trusts were established by Sir Ratan Tata and Sir Dorabji Tata for public welfare and that trustees were custodians of their assets, not owners. He cited their founding objectives, including poverty alleviation and safeguarding Indian culture, and said the institutions should remain focused on serving the people of India.Jimmy traced the current governance differences to amendments made to Tata Sons’ Articles of Association around 2013-14, which he said had fundamentally altered the relationship between the charitable trusts and the operating company.He argued that the earlier framework kept the welfare trusts separate from Tata Sons’ commercial operations, while subsequent amendments gave the Tata Trusts chairman veto powers and the ability to place directors, undermining the collective authority of the board.He also questioned differences in trustee tenure rules, alleging that they had compromised independence and enabled the marginalisation of dissenting trustees.Also Read: Noel Tata warns Tata Sons listing could put profits ahead of philanthropy, says it may change the ‘Tata way’Citing Venu Srinivasan, whose term expires in December, he alleged that Srinivasan was being targeted for opposing the induction of Noel Tata’s son into SRTT. He also referred to the earlier removal of Vijay Singh.Jimmy contrasted the current situation with the past, when independent figures such as Nani Palkhivala, Gautam Sarabhai, Homi Sethna and Homi Bhabha served as trustees.On the differences over Chandrasekaran’s continuation as Tata Sons chairman, Jimmy praised his leadership, saying he had turned around companies burdened by severe debt and delivered record earnings and substantial dividend payouts.“Despite Chandrasekaran receiving overwhelming support (including 4–1 in Tata Sons board and a unanimous resolution passed by Tata Trusts), Noel sought to block him arbitrarily by invoking the onerous veto provisions in the amended Articles of Association without providing any justification or accountability,” he said.Jimmy’s comments come amid a widening rift between Noel, chairman of Tata Trusts, and the Tata Sons board over Chandrasekaran’s reappointment, the proposed listing of the holding company and the group’s governance structure.Tata Trusts collectively owns about 66% of Tata Sons, with SRTT holding 23.56%. Its position is central to decisions concerning the future of the holding company and the wider conglomerate.Jimmy said listing Tata Sons was critical to improving transparency and accountability and restoring the separation between the charitable trusts and the commercial operations of the group.“Listing would dismantle the pervasive culture of secrecy, impose statutory accountability, and necessitate rewriting the onerous Articles of Association to restore the pre-1989 separation between business operations and welfare trusts,” he said.He also warned against any attempt to restructure Tata Sons into smaller entities to avoid regulatory listing requirements, saying this would be contrary to public and shareholder interests.Jimmy called on the RBI to enforce strict timelines for listing and urged the government and the Charity Commissioner to intervene to protect the original objectives of the trusts.The RBI has classified Tata Sons as an upper-layer non-banking financial company (NBFC), requiring it to list its equity shares on a recognised stock exchange within three years of being identified in that category. The central bank has rejected Tata Sons’ application to surrender its core investment company registration, requiring it to comply with the regulatory framework applicable to upper-layer NBFCs.Also Read: Tata International appoints T V Narendran as Chairman and Noel N Tata as Chairman Emeritus effective November 12Jimmy has been a trustee of SRTT since 1989 and is one of its three perpetual trustees, the others being Noel Tata and Jehangir Jehangir. He is the younger son of Naval Tata and his first wife Sooni Commissariat. Noel Tata is Naval Tata’s son from his second marriage to Simone Dunoyer.Jimmy, who lives in Pune, has historically preferred correspondence to participation in trust meetings. During a 2016 interview, he showed reporters a file containing hundreds of letters through which he had communicated his views to trustees and board members.He is also the second-largest individual shareholder of Tata Sons after Noel Tata, with a 0.81% stake, or 3,262 shares, according to estimates based on investment banking data.
